facts.fact: The US Country Commercial Guide says MTNIMA, the Mauritanian digital ministry, has published the National AI Strategy (2025-2029); the guide gives no date for the publication, so the document's published date of 2026-02-10 is used.

note: Regional index page; the held text says nothing of a Mauritanian national AI strategy (Mauritania appears only as a planned recipient of cross-border compute).

facts.fact: Mauritania's Ministry of Digital Transformation, Innovation and Modernization of Administration published the National AI Strategy 2024-2029 marked Draft (April 2024), with 5 strategic priorities, 12 objectives and 30 measures.

Mauritania's Ministry of Digital Transformation, Innovation and Modernisation of Administration issued the National AI Strategy 2025-2029 in a final Arabic edition with thirteen axes; the document gives no adoption date, so as_of is its published month (2024-07).

note: Its governance chapter says a sub-committee of the Supreme Council for Digitalisation will be established to monitor the strategy: a future body, not yet named as set up.
Cabinet text concerns minors' access to social media; no AI strategy stated.

facts.fact: Ecofin Agency states Mauritania has a national artificial intelligence strategy for 2025-2029 providing for applications in healthcare, education, agriculture and transportation.

note: Document mentions the ministry's AI strategy 2025-2029 but not whether it is adopted, drafted, funded or given a body.

facts.fact: The minister of digital transformation opened a workshop presenting Mauritania's national AI strategy (2025-2029; 6 priorities, 16 objectives, 38 actions), prepared with GIZ support, and said it will be implemented soon; no adoption is stated.

facts.fact: The two-day Nouakchott international AI conference, opened by the higher-education ministry on 26 May 2025, was to present the national AI strategy and hold a round table on it; no adoption is stated.
The digital transformation ministry held a one-day consultation workshop in Nouakchott on the content of Mauritania's national AI strategy, opened by Minister Mohamed Abdellahi Louli.
The Mauritanian presentation to the ITU lists among the ministry's initiatives the elaboration of an artificial intelligence strategy 2025-2029, with no adoption stated.

note: A national AI strategy is named among the agenda's supporting strategies, with no word on drafting or adoption.
